title: Research: policy-as-code and policy-based access control for agents (OPA/Rego, Cedar, Azure Policy)
goal: Answer with the kb tools first and official sources for the rest, writing facts through /kb-research with a new topic agents/policy-as-code where no article fits: How does Open Policy Agent evaluate an authorization query with Rego and distribute policy bundles? How do Cedar policies express permit, forbid and attribute conditions? What does Amazon Verified Permissions add to Cedar? What can Azure Policy deny, audit or remediate for resources an automation creates, with its definitions kept as code?
